findings.cause: No validation in the handler, and one catch-all reply.
findings.dependencies: Error monitoring; the screens' messages.
findings.verification: Probe section 3: 19 server errors before, 3 after (the 3 are B-006). Unit test "a change aimed at a missing record…".
findings.where: src/backend/src/middleware/safeErrors.js; src/backend/src/lib/db.js; routes/workCenters.js, assets.js, maintenanceOrders.js, salesRoutes.js, executive.js, materialTrackingRoutes.js, partner/adminRoutes.js
findings.evidence: qa/sim/baseline-probe.mjs section 3 on commit 2d801ff: 19 of 275 write routes answered an empty body or an unknown id with a 500.
findings.expected: An unknown record is a 404. Missing or wrong values are a 400. A 500 means the server is at fault.
findings.actual: These handlers catch every failure and answer 500, including "that record does not exist".
findings.impact: Staff see "failed" with no reason; monitoring cannot tell a typing mistake from an outage.
findings.correction: The reply layer now turns a failed change into 404 when the record was not there and 400 when the database layer refused the values, and logs the detail. One handler (new scenario) checks its name. Field-by-field validation in these handlers is still owed (see B-007).
findings.requiredTests: Unit test for the rule; probe section 3 with a ceiling that can only go down.

findings.cause: Prototype stores that were moved from memory into tables without being redesigned.
findings.dependencies: D-024, S-021, I-011 and the open decision card "Choose which stock list is the real one".
findings.statusNote: Owner's decision 1, 2026-11-13: The stock items list that orders, receiving, shipping and invoices update is the real stock, and sales orders are the real orders. The second stock list and the order hub are to be connected to them or retired, never built on separately. This is the engineer's recommendation, adopted under the owner's instruction to use the best logical choice. Decided by the owner (decision 1): the stock items list and sales orders are the real ones. Phase 2 put both second copies under a department rule and inside the gates; it did not connect or retire them. Phase 3 audited the two stores and did not migrate them. The QA database holds only fixture rows in them; what the live stores hold cannot be seen from here, and moving records nobody has inspected into the order and stock tables would be changing business data on a guess. Phase 5: the Order Hub screen is retired (S-021). The second stock list and its JSON store remain; they belong with inventory in Phase 6. Phase 6: the second stock list can no longer be written. POST /api/v1/inventory/adjust, /rfid-scan, /transfers and /transfers/:id/status answer 410 RETIRED with where to go instead; its reads remain so nothing on screen breaks. The order hub half was handled in Phase 5 (S-021). What remains: remove the v1 reads and their demo data once the screens that read them are pointed at the stock items list (Phase 9 screen work).
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs: "the retired v1 stock writes change nothing", "the old transfer address still works but now ships, and the old v1 transfer writes are retired".
findings.module: Second stock list, order hub, stop work
findings.where: routes/inventoryV1.js + inventoryV1Store.js; routes/orderHubRoutes.js + orderHubStore.js; routes/stopWork.js + stopWorkStore.js
findings.evidence: Code read. Each keeps whole records as one JSON value per row. inventoryV1.js reloads five whole tables at the start of every request (refresh(), 13 call sites), changes the copies in memory and writes rows back one at a time with no transaction. /api/v1/inventory has its own adjust and transfer routes on stock that orders and shipping never see. The order hub has its own contacts, RFQs, quotes, orders and jobs.
findings.expected: One stock ledger and one order record, with database rules on them.
findings.actual: Two stock lists and two order pipelines. The second of each has no database rule on any value, and two requests at once can overwrite each other.
findings.impact: Stock adjusted or transferred in the second list changes nothing the business ships from. At volume, each request to it reads every row.
findings.correction: The owner chooses the real one of each pair. Then the other is removed or made a view of the first.
findings.requiredTests: A two-requests-at-once test on whichever store is kept; the audit shows one stock list.
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer

findings.cause: No move table for operations.
findings.dependencies: Time tracking, schedule, job status.
findings.statusNote: Owner's decision 8, 2026-11-15: A step cannot start until the steps before it are finished. It is one setting (production.rules.stepsInOrder), on by default. Phase 7: confirmed by running it (L-004) and corrected. A step must be started before it is finished, a finished step cannot be started again, and a pause needs a running clock. The owner decided on 2026-11-15 that steps run in their planned order (decision 8). Whether a finished step may be reopened for rework is now finding L-020.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "steps run in their planned order", "a step that was never started cannot be finished", "finishing the last step sends the job to inspection once; finishing it again changes nothing"; qa/sim/phase2-integrity.mjs; src/backend/test/phase7Rules.test.js.
findings.evidence: Code read: neither checks the operation's present status. A completed operation can be started again; an operation can be completed twice or without having started.
findings.expected: An operation follows not-started, running, paused, complete (lib/workflowRules.js does this for jobs, orders and shipments).
findings.actual: Any call is accepted.
findings.impact: Actual start and end times and the time logs can be overwritten; labor time is unreliable.
findings.correction: A move table for operations in lib/workflowRules.js. Whether a completed operation may be reopened for rework is the owner's rule (extends M-017).
findings.requiredTests: Unit tests for the table; a sweep check per refused move.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence

findings.cause: The hosted server runs per request; nothing runs between requests.
findings.dependencies: Any future integration that needs scheduled work (email, statements, replenishment, overdue invoices).
findings.statusNote: Needs a scheduled trigger on the host, which is the owner's setting Phase 4: delivery is now durable (see H-002): a failed event waits in the database for 1, 5, 30 and 120 minutes and is kept as failed after five tries. The retries are carried out when the scheduled address is called; setting that schedule on the host is B-019.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs, group "Event processing and background jobs".
findings.evidence: Code read: a failed delivery is marked RETRYING with a next-retry time, and processPendingRetries() would resend it. Nothing calls that function (no import, no schedule), and the server has no scheduler, queue or background worker of any kind.
findings.expected: A failed delivery is retried.
findings.actual: It is marked for retry and never sent again.
findings.impact: A partner that was briefly unreachable never receives the event.
findings.correction: A scheduled trigger on the host that calls the retry function. Setting up a schedule on the host is the owner's.
findings.requiredTests: A test that fails a delivery, runs the retry and sees it delivered.
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication

findings.cause: Per-request hosting and no provider chosen.
findings.statusNote: Phase 4: the scheduled work now exists as one address, GET or POST /api/internal/tasks/run, protected by a secret (CRON_SECRET). It sends waiting partner events and clears old request keys, is safe to call from several places at once, and records when it last ran; the Integrations screen shows that time and has a "Run now" button. Blocked on two host settings that are the owner's: (1) set CRON_SECRET to a long random value; (2) add a schedule that calls the address every 5 minutes with "Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>". It was not added to vercel.json because a schedule the plan does not allow can fail the deployment. Until then nothing is lost: events are sent right after each action, and a failed one waits for "Run now".
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "the scheduled run needs its secret, does the periodic work and records that it ran", "five delivery runs at the same moment send each event once". The host schedule itself is NOT VERIFIED.
findings.evidence: Discovery: no scheduler, queue, worker, event bus or email or text provider exists in the server code. Nothing is sent to a customer or a colleague by the system (D-033, D-034); exception records are created only when a person or a request creates them; an expired quote or an overdue invoice is worked out when someone looks at it and nobody is told.
findings.expected: To be decided per function.
findings.actual: Everything happens only when someone opens a screen or presses a button.
findings.impact: No reminders, no escalation, no automatic status by date, no customer notification.
findings.correction: Choose the provider and the host schedule; then build each timed function.
findings.requiredTests: Per function.

findings.cause: The quick sale was built as a priced receipt on top of orders and invoices; stock for items priced each was left out and the void marker was put in the notes.
findings.dependencies: The owner: are shelf items counted stock? I-016 (no stock adjustment).
findings.statusNote: Owner's decision 6, 2026-11-13: A counter sale reduces stock, and a void puts it back. Phase 2, owner's decision 6: a counter sale takes its pieces from the shelf stock of the selling branch and a void puts them back. What is still missing is a way to receive shelf items by the piece (C-011), so in practice a product has shelf stock only once that exists.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase2-integrity.mjs: 13 checks, including three sales at once for the last pieces and one sale sent three times.
findings.evidence: Code read and the QA database after three simulation cycles: a finished counter quick sale is a COMPLETE order whose lines say they shipped, with no shipment, no stock movement and no change to any stock level. A voided sale is still COMPLETE; the void is the word VOIDED added to the order notes, plus a credit memo and a refund. qa/tools/db-facts.mjs counts these lines separately.
findings.expected: A rule, written down: either shelf items are counted stock and a sale reduces it (and a void puts it back), or they are not counted and the system says so. A void that reports can filter on without reading free text.
findings.actual: Shelf items sold at the counter never reduce stock. Any report that filters on order status counts a voided sale as a completed one; only the counter's own daily figures read the note.
findings.impact: Shelf stock cannot be trusted if it is ever counted in the system. Sales reports by order status overstate by the voided sales (the money side is correct: the credit memo and refund exist).
findings.correction: After the decision: record a stock movement on sale and on void, and give a voided sale its own status or flag.
findings.requiredTests: Simulation: a counter sale reduces the shelf item and a void restores it; reports exclude voided sales.
findings.phase: Inventory and purchasing

findings.workflow: Starting and completing operations; moving a job
findings.cause: Read, decide, write with no lock and no condition on the write.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase2-integrity.mjs: four race checks of 8 rounds each, plus the cancelled-job and repeated-completion checks. All fail on the code before the fix.
findings.phase: Phase 2: architecture and code quality
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase2-integrity.mjs on the code before the fix. Two operators completing the last two operations of a job at the same moment: in 8 of 8 rounds the job stayed IN_PROCESS for ever, because each request counted the other operation as still open. Completing an operation of a cancelled job moved the cancelled job to WAITING_QC. Two people moving one job at once both succeeded and the history did not match the job.
findings.expected: Whatever the timing, the job, its operations and its history agree, and a cancelled job stays cancelled.
findings.actual: Three ways for the shop-floor record to end up wrong under ordinary simultaneous use.
findings.impact: Jobs stuck in process that are in fact finished; cancelled work reappearing in the inspection queue.
findings.correction: Completing an operation locks the dispatch job and the job first. Operations of a finished or cancelled job are refused (409). A repeated completion changes nothing. A job status move applies only if the job is still in the status it was checked in, and is saved with its history line.
findings.requiredTests: Race rounds for each case, checked against the database.

findings.cause: No idempotency key.
findings.dependencies: A new table for request keys.
findings.statusNote: Phase 3: a RequestKey table with a unique rule on (user and route, key); middleware on every changing route that honours an Idempotency-Key header; the screens send a key for every request that creates a document (src/frontend/src/api/requestKey.js). A repeat gets the first answer back; the same key with a different body is refused (422); a refused request is not remembered. Phase 4: the request-key middleware is now exercised on shipments (create, dispatch, deliver), payments, receipts, transfers, credits, work order completion, purchase orders, quote acceptance and counter sales, and by partners; two defects in it were found and fixed (H-003, H-004). A browser test asserts that the screens send the key and reuse it on a retry.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs: the same order sent three times at once with one key saves one order and the retry is marked as a replay; different body 422; another user's same key is separate; a stale claim is taken over after a minute. test/requestKeys.test.js (3 tests). Order creation only was exercised through the API; the web checkout and order intake use the same middleware and were not separately run (NOT VERIFIED for those two routes).
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: Code read: none of the three accepts a request key. The simulation probe "10 simultaneous orders all saved with distinct numbers" shows identical bodies are each saved. The counter quick sale is the one sale route that recognises a repeat (by its sale id).
findings.expected: A request repeated after a timeout or a double press creates one order.
findings.actual: It creates two. Only the screens guard against it, by disabling the button while saving.
findings.impact: A duplicate order on a slow connection, found later by a person.
findings.correction: An Idempotency-Key header on order creation, stored with a unique rule per user, answering a repeat with the first reply.
findings.requiredTests: The same key twice, in sequence and at once: one order, the same answer.

findings.cause: creditInvoice and recordRefund open their own transactions and cannot be nested as written.
findings.dependencies: F-series billing functions.
findings.statusNote: Phase 3: creditInvoice accepts steps that run inside its own transaction. A void now claims the sale, returns the shelf stock, writes the credit memo and records the refund in one transaction.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs: a credit whose last step is forced to fail leaves no memo, no refund, no history line, and undoes the step before it; a sale voided twice at once is voided once, with one credit memo, one stock return and money netting to zero.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: Code read: the void is claimed and the stock returned in one transaction (Phase 2). The credit memo and the refund are then made by two further calls, each its own transaction.
findings.expected: A void is all or nothing.
findings.actual: A failure after the claim leaves a sale marked void, its stock returned, and no credit memo or refund.
findings.impact: Rare (it needs a failure between two calls), and visible: the sale shows as void with money still taken.
findings.correction: Let creditInvoice and recordRefund accept an open transaction, and run the whole void in one.
findings.requiredTests: A failure forced after the claim leaves the sale exactly as it was.

findings.cause: Receiving was built for metal by weight.
findings.dependencies: I-016 (count and adjustment). The owner: may an item with no shelf stock on file be sold? Today it may, with the note.
findings.statusNote: Phase 3 did not change Coil.heatId or gradeId. Making them optional changes what every stock screen and trace report may assume, and the rule for piece goods is the owner's. No database change was made on a guess. Phase 6: shelf goods are received by the piece (form SUPPLY) against a product in the catalog, with no heat or grade; the stock is counted in EA. A database check (Coil_heat_and_grade_unless_supply, SQL Editor file 12) keeps heat and grade required for every other form. The counter sale and its void already move piece stock (Phase 2 and 5).
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs: "shelf goods are received by the piece against a product, with no heat or grade", "shelf goods need a whole number of pieces and a product that is in the catalog"; qa/sim/security.mjs section 20 ships a web line of pieces from a received lot; src/backend/test/phase6Rules.test.js.
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.evidence: Code read: receiving creates stock by weight only (unit LB) and needs a heat and a grade. No route creates stock counted in pieces. The QA database holds 333 stock levels, all in LB.

findings.expected: A line is never reserved beyond what it still needs, and a cancelled order holds no stock.
findings.actual: The open quantity and the order status were read before the transaction and not checked again inside it.
findings.impact: Stock tied up that nobody can see a reason for; available stock understated; in the cancelled case nothing ever releases it.
findings.correction: The reservation locks the order row first, then reads the status and the line's open quantity inside the transaction. A cancellation waits for it and releases what it saved.
findings.requiredTests: Both races, six rounds each; eight reservations at once on one item.

findings.cause: Processing moves no stock (M-016), so there is no step at which the parent is reduced.

Recording a remnant against its parent takes the remnant's weight off the parent in the same transaction, with a movement on the parent that names the piece (lib/receiving.js, takeFromParent). A remnant heavier than what is free on the parent is refused.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs "a remnant entered against its parent...": parent 6000 to 5948.75, movement on the parent, the two together still 6000; a heavier remnant refused. On the old code the parent stays at 6000.

Sending puts the item's free quantity in an in-transit bucket at the sending branch (reservations and holds travel with it); it cannot be sold, reserved, cut, corrected or sent again. The receiving branch books it in; anything short, missing or damaged is held with a note until a manager or the inventory manager settles it. The sender can call it back before it arrives. Tables StockTransfer and StockTransferLine, column Inventory.qtyInTransit, and the balance identity now includes in transit (SQL Editor file 12).
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs: the 17 "Interbranch transfers" scenarios and the transfer scenarios under "Concurrency, security and recovery"; qa/sim/ui-phase6.cjs: transfers received from the screen; src/backend/test/phase6Rules.test.js (4 tests); qa/tools/db-facts.mjs: five transfer checks at 0. findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer

Owner decision of 2026-11-13: one item may feed several work orders if the system tracks it. It now does: a work order may be raised on an item that is available or reserved, and each takes only what is free (or reserved for its own line) at the moment it completes, under a lock on the item's balance. The item can never go below zero.

findings.correction: Decided with M-016.

findings.cause: Never added to these two routes.

findings.cause: An ordinary table.
findings.dependencies: The owner's database roles on the host.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: Catalogue read: no trigger and no rule protects AuditLog; the application's database role may update and delete it. Two code paths do: a duplicate counter sale deletes the history lines of the copy it removes, and revoking an override updates its line. Changes to an order's fields other than status, edits to a stock item, and the release of reservations by a cancellation are not itemised.
findings.expected: History is append-only; critical field changes carry before and after values.
findings.actual: History can be rewritten by any code with database access.
findings.impact: The audit trail is evidence only as long as nobody with access wants otherwise.
findings.correction: Revoke update and delete on AuditLog from the application role, or add a trigger that refuses them; change the two code paths to add a line instead; add before and after values for order and stock item edits.
findings.requiredTests: An update and a delete of an audit row are refused by the database.

deferral.reason: It needs a change to database roles on the host, which are the owner's, and it is the subject of the security phase.
deferral.targetPhase: Phase 10: security and infrastructure
deferral.correction: As above.

deferral.verification: A database scenario that tries both.

findings.cause: Schema.
findings.statusNote: Takes effect in the live database when the owner applies database update 8.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs: a quote written at one branch answers 404 to a sales login at another and is absent from its list; the order made from it carries the same branch. test/branchScope.test.js: 2 new tests. SQL Editor file run twice on the scale copy.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: C-009: a sales login at one branch could read every branch's quotes, because the tables had no branch.
findings.expected: A quote belongs to the branch of the person who wrote it.

findings.cause: A contains-search across three tables cannot use an ordinary index; Job has no branch column of its own.

No index was added: the instruction forbids one without evidence of need, and all are inside the half-second target.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.module: Stock items, stock search, heat trace
findings.evidence: Measured on the scale copy (100,233 stock items, 72,541 jobs, 85 branches; qa/results/phase3-plans.txt): the stock search reads every stock item (sequential scan, 140 ms); a branch's job count reads every job in the company (parallel sequential scan, 25 ms) because a job reaches its branch through its order, its work center or its creator.
findings.expected: The cost of a branch screen grows with the branch, not the company.
findings.actual: Both grow in step with the whole company's data. Both are far inside the half-second target today.
findings.impact: None now. At ten times the volume the search would take over a second.
findings.correction: A trigram index and a search limited to one column at a time; a branch column on Job, kept by the same code that sets its order and work center.
findings.requiredTests: The same two measurements at one million rows.

deferral.targetPhase: Phase 11: performance and full simulation cycles
deferral.correction: As above, if the measurement at ten times the volume shows the need.

deferral.verification: qa/perf/phase3-plans.sh and qa/perf/branch-bench.mjs on a larger copy.

findings.cause: One include clause for list and detail.

No screen was switched to it in this phase. Phase 5: reviewed for the screens. No screen lists GET /api/orders: the All Orders screen reads the order intake list, which it shows master and detail (the selected order's lines), and the home page reads /api/dashboard. The summary view of /api/orders, built in Phase 4, is what a list without lines uses, and is checked again in Phase 5.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase5-sales.mjs: "the order list answers a page in summary form" (smaller reply, line count, no lines).
findings.phase: Phase 5: customer lifecycle, sales operations, CRM, quoting, order intake, POS, ecommerce and customer portal

findings.expected: A list sends what the list shows.
findings.actual: Each order comes with its full lines and customer record.

findings.cause: Host settings are the owner's.
findings.dependencies: The owner.
findings.statusNote: Blocked on the owner reading two host settings. Nothing was changed.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.where: DATABASE_URL on the host (the owner's setting)
findings.evidence: The repository sets no pool size or timeout; the database client's default is used (16 connections observed under load on a 4-processor machine). On the host each serverless instance opens its own pool. Whether DATABASE_URL points at the provider's connection pooler, and with what limits, cannot be read from here.
findings.expected: A stated limit per instance and a pooler in front of the database, so that many instances cannot exhaust it.
findings.actual: Unknown.
findings.impact: If the direct address is used, a burst of traffic that starts many instances can use every connection the database allows.
findings.correction: Confirm that DATABASE_URL is the pooler address (port 6543 on Supabase, with pgbouncer=true and a connection_limit) and DIRECT_URL the direct one.
findings.requiredTests: A load test against a staging copy.

findings.cause: Not decided.
findings.statusNote: Question for the owner: how many years of audit history and stock movements must stay online? Owner decision of 2026-11-13: five years for now, with warnings to archive. GET /api/admin/retention counts records older than the period, and those within six months of it, for nine record types, and returns a warning. Managers see the warning on the user administration screen. The period is 5 years unless an AppSetting 'retention.years' says otherwise. Nothing is removed or moved: archiving itself is not built and would need the owner's approval of what is archived and where.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs "history older than five years raises an archive warning, and nothing is removed"; test/stockChanges.test.js (cutoff and level).
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: No retention or archive rule exists for any table. RequestKey rows are removed after 24 hours by the middleware itself. Sizes on the scale copy: the whole database is 325 MB at 72,240 orders.
findings.expected: A rule for how long history is kept and where it goes.
findings.actual: Everything is kept for ever in the working tables.
findings.impact: None for years at the measured growth; a decision, not a defect.
findings.correction: The owner sets the periods; archive tables or partitions follow only if the volume needs them.
findings.requiredTests: None until the rule exists.

findings.workflow: Numbering of orders, shipments, invoices and other documents
findings.cause: Every simultaneous request started from the same count and walked forward together.
findings.statusNote: Document numbers can have gaps. If the owner needs invoice numbers with no gaps, that is a different mechanism (a counter row locked per series) and a decision. As before for orders, shipments, jobs and work orders: a number is never repeated and none is lost under 80 simultaneous saves, though a number can be skipped. Owner decision of 2026-11-13 for invoices: never skipped or repeated. Invoice and credit memo numbers now come from a DocumentCounter row that is advanced inside the transaction that saves the document, at the moment it is written, so a save that fails or is refused gives its number back. Counter sales take their invoice number from the same series (they were INV-QS-<order number> before). A counter sale sent twice is held by a lock on the sale id instead of being written and deleted. Numbers issued before this change keep whatever gaps they have.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs group 7: twelve invoices raised at once take twelve consecutive numbers; a credit that fails after taking its number, a refused credit and an order with nothing to bill take none; a counter sale sent three times at once is one sale with the next number. db-facts: counter equals the highest number on file, no number repeated. SQL Editor file 20261113220000_document_counters run twice on the 85-branch copy.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.where: src/backend/src/lib/numbering.js (used by 15 route and service files)
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs on the code before the fix: 80 orders entered at the same moment, 72 saved and 8 answered "Failed to create order" (server log: "Could not assign a unique number"). Unit test on the same code: a series that has had rows deleted, so that its row count is more than 25 below its highest number, can never issue another number.
findings.expected: Eighty branches can save at once, and a series keeps working after rows are deleted.
findings.actual: The next number was the row count plus one, tried 25 times in step with every other request.
findings.impact: Lost orders at a busy moment; and a document type that stops working for good once enough rows have been deleted (a duplicate counter sale deletes its order).
findings.correction: After two collisions the search waits a random moment, counts again and steps ahead by a random distance that doubles. A series may skip numbers; the unique rule in the database guarantees none repeats.
findings.requiredTests: 80 at once; a series whose count lags its highest number by 300.

findings.cause: The column was added in Phase 2 to a table with rows.
findings.dependencies: The owner gives every staff login a home branch and assigns the orders that have none.
findings.statusNote: Phase 5: quotes, accepted quotes, web orders, order intake and counter sales now set the order's branch (J-001, J-005, S-008). The column stays optional for all-branch logins with no home branch; orders with no branch after the final gate run: 59 after the simulation and 62 after all scenarios (63 at the end of Phase 4); the rest are seed orders and orders entered by all-branch logins with no home branch.
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.evidence: db-facts on the QA database: orders with no branch 59 (the demo seed) rising to 62 after the scenarios, because an order entered by a login with no home branch gets none; 2 staff logins have no home branch.
findings.expected: Every order has a branch.
findings.actual: The column is optional, so that existing rows and all-branch logins keep working.
findings.impact: An order with no branch is seen only by all-branch roles.
findings.correction: After the backfill: make Order.locationId required, and refuse an order from a login with no branch unless it names one.
findings.requiredTests: db-facts "orders with no branch" is 0; a database scenario for the refusal.

deferral.targetPhase: Phase 10: security and infrastructure
deferral.correction: As above.

deferral.acceptance: No order without a branch; the column is NOT NULL.
deferral.verification: db-facts in the gates; the migration run twice on a copy.

findings.cause: Dispatch consumes reservations and does nothing when there are none.
findings.dependencies: I-016 (no stock adjustment), M-016.
findings.statusNote: Question for the owner: may an order ship when no stock has been reserved for it? If yes, in which cases (direct from the mill, buy-outs), and how should the heat be recorded? Owner decision of 2026-11-13: refuse. A shipment that carries more than is reserved for its line is refused at dispatch (routes/shipments.js, consumeReserved), with a message that says to reserve the stock first. Nothing is saved for any line of the shipment. Every shipment therefore names its stock items, and through them the heat, and reduces the balance. The shop-floor Ship button goes through the same step.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs "a shipment with nothing reserved, or less reserved than it carries, is refused and changes nothing": nothing reserved is refused; half a pound short is refused; fully reserved goes, with movements naming the item. db-facts check for dispatched shipment items not covered by stock movements is 0 after the gate run. On the old code the first check fails (dispatch was accepted).
findings.phase: Phase 3: database integrity, transactional correctness, performance and 80-location scalability
findings.where: src/backend/src/routes/shipments.js (consumeReserved: "Stock with no reservation is left alone")
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs: a shipment of 300 lb for an order line with nothing reserved is dispatched and invoiced; no stock movement is written, no stock item is named and no balance goes down. ShipmentItem has no column for the stock item; the only link from a shipment to an item, and so to its heat, is the movement written when reserved stock is consumed.
findings.expected: Every pound that leaves is taken from a named stock item, so the heat can be traced to the customer and the shelf balance is right; or the shipment is marked as material that was never in stock (a direct shipment from the mill).
findings.actual: Shipping reserved stock is fully recorded. Shipping without a reservation is accepted and records nothing about the material.
findings.impact: For such a shipment a mill certificate cannot be matched to the customer from the records, and the stock on the books stays too high.
findings.correction: The engineer's recommendation: refuse to dispatch a line that is not fully reserved, unless the order line is marked as shipped direct from a supplier.
findings.requiredTests: Dispatch with a part reservation is refused; a direct shipment is accepted and marked; the database check for uncovered shipment items returns 0.

findings.cause: No version or updated-at check on edits.
findings.statusNote: Phase 4: PUT /api/orders/:id accepts expectedUpdatedAt and refuses an edit made from an older copy with 409 and the code STALE_EDIT. It is opt-in, so no existing caller breaks. No screen edits an order header today, so no screen sends it; the other edit routes are unchanged. Phase 5: reviewed. No screen edits an order through PUT /api/orders/:id (the call in api/index.js has no user). Orders are edited on the order entry screen through PATCH /api/orders/intake/:id, which does not check the version. The API check from Phase 4 is tested again in Phase 5. Phase 9: the screens' order save helper now sends the version it read, and the server refuses a save made from an older one (409). No screen edits an order's header fields today, so no user can meet the fault through the product. The other edit routes (customers, stock items, work orders) are unchanged.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase9-ui.cjs: "the order save helper sends the version it read, and the server refuses a save made from an older one".
findings.phase: Phase 9: user experience, visual design and accessibility
findings.where: PUT /api/orders/:id and the other edit routes
findings.evidence: Code read and qa/sim/phase3-db.mjs: a change of status is conditional on the status the editor saw, so of two simultaneous status changes one wins and the other is told (409). A change to other fields (dates, notes, ship-to) carries no version: two people saving different edits both succeed and the later one silently replaces the earlier where they touch the same field.
findings.expected: The second editor is told the record changed.
findings.actual: Status is protected; other fields are last write wins.
findings.impact: An edit can be lost without notice. No quantity or amount is at risk: totals are recomputed and checked by the database.
findings.correction: Send the record's updatedAt with an edit and refuse the edit if it has changed (409).
findings.requiredTests: Two edits at once: one 200, one 409.

deferral.reason: The remaining edit routes need the same server check, which is reliability work.
deferral.targetPhase: Phase 10: security and infrastructure
deferral.correction: Require the version on every edit route and send it from every edit form.
deferral.acceptance: Two people editing the same record: the second is told and loses nothing silently.
deferral.verification: A two-user scenario per record type.

findings.workflow: Customers, carriers and suppliers reading and acting through the API
findings.cause: Written against an earlier idea of the schema and never run.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "a carrier reports delivery through the partner API", "a supplier reads and acknowledges only purchase orders placed with it", "what a partner reads equals what staff see", "a carrier sees only its own loads, and no prices", "scopes and partner types are enforced on every kind of route", "the partner API keeps one shape for lists, one for errors". On the code before, the same calls answered 500.
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: First success-path run of the partner API in this program, with a real partner key and token: almost every route answered 500. The handlers filtered on columns that do not exist, set statuses that do not exist and read relations by the wrong name. Where a carrier route could have run, it changed a shipment directly and skipped the dispatch and delivery rules staff go through. Extends C-002 from carriers to all three partner kinds.
findings.expected: A partner reads its own records and acts through the same rules as staff.
findings.actual: The API could not be used; had it been repaired in place it would have bypassed stock, order and invoice rules.
findings.impact: No partner integration could go live; a repaired-in-place carrier update could mark a load delivered that never left.
findings.correction: The three route files were rewritten on the real schema and on the staff steps themselves: a carrier report calls the same deliver and move steps as the shipping desk and can never dispatch; a customer creates a request for quote and accepts or declines a quote through the same functions as the sales desk; a supplier reads and acknowledges its own purchase orders. Shared parsing, paging and refusal shape in routes/partner/common.js.
findings.requiredTests: Success path and refusal path for every working route; isolation between two partners of the same kind.

findings.cause: No durable queue and no link from the staff routes.
findings.statusNote: The retry schedule runs only when the host calls the scheduled address (B-019, the owner's setting). Without it, an event is still sent right after the action, and a failed one waits until an administrator presses "Run now" on the Integrations screen.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs, group "Event processing and background jobs": 13 scenarios, all pass. SQL Editor file 10 ran twice on the 85-branch copy with duplicate rows planted: the later duplicates were renamed, none deleted, and the second run changed nothing.
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: Code read and test: a failed delivery was marked for retry and the retry lived only in the memory of the server instance, so it was lost on restart and never resumed (B-018). No staff action raised an event at all: a dispatch at the shipping desk told no partner. Nothing stopped the same event being recorded twice for a subscriber. A row was written after the business change, so a crash between the two lost the event.
findings.expected: A business change and the events about it are saved together; each event reaches each subscriber once, is retried on a schedule, stops after a limit and can be sent again by a person.
findings.actual: Events were best effort, raised only by partner calls, and lost on any failure.
findings.impact: A customer or carrier system that relies on events silently misses dispatches, deliveries and invoices.
findings.correction: The existing WebhookDelivery table is used as an outbox. The row is written inside the transaction that makes the change (order confirmed, status changed, shipment dispatched, delivered, exception, invoice issued). Delivery claims a row with a conditional update, so several servers can run it at once; failures wait 1, 5, 30 and 120 minutes; after five tries the event is kept as failed; an administrator can send it again; a unique rule on (subscription, event) makes a second recording impossible (migration 20261113230000_webhook_delivery_once). No new infrastructure.
findings.requiredTests: Delivered once; refused change leaves no event; backoff honoured; dead letter after five; replay; five runs at once; claim taken over after a crash.

findings.workflow: Request keys on the partner API
findings.cause: The middleware is mounted globally, before the partner token is read.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "the same key with a different request is refused, and the same key from another person is their own request" and the partner checks in "a quote accepted by the customer and the sales desk at the same moment makes one order".
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.category: Security: one caller receiving another's answer
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs on the code before: two different partners sent the same Idempotency-Key to the same address. The request-key middleware ran before partner sign-in and filed both under "anonymous", so the second partner was answered with the first partner's stored reply.
findings.expected: A key belongs to the caller who sent it.
findings.actual: All partner calls shared one scope.
findings.impact: One partner could be shown another partner's created record, and its own request was not carried out.
findings.correction: At the global mount the middleware steps aside for partner addresses; the partner route stack runs it after sign-in, scoped to the partner.
findings.requiredTests: Same key from two partners: two separate requests.

findings.cause: The key was released on connection close rather than when the handler finished.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "the answer is lost after the server saved: the retry gets the same order back, not a second one", "a request whose first attempt died is taken over once, not twice". qa/sim/ui-integration.cjs: "answer lost after saving (new shipment)": one shipment, same key on both attempts.
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs on the code before: a client sent an order with a key and hung up before the answer. The middleware released the key when the connection closed, while the handler was still running. The client's retry with the same key was treated as new and a second order was saved.
findings.expected: A retry after a lost answer gets the first result.
findings.actual: Two orders.
findings.impact: Duplicate orders, shipments or payments exactly when the network is poor, which is when people retry.
findings.correction: A dropped connection no longer releases the key. The handler finishes and its answer is stored; the retry is answered with it. A claim whose server died is taken over after a minute, once.
findings.requiredTests: Send and hang up, then retry: one record.

findings.workflow: Calls to outside services (speech, AI providers, partner addresses)
findings.cause: Each call site was written on its own.
findings.statusNote: The breaker and its counters are per server instance (H-012). No real provider was called in any test; the real providers' behaviour is NOT VERIFIED.
findings.verification: test/outbound.test.js (8 tests). qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs, group "Webhooks and external service failures": 11 scenarios, including "the speech provider hangs: the user gets a plain answer at the time limit and stays signed in" and "the server log holds request ids and reasons, and no key, token or signing secret".
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.category: Reliability and security: no time limit; provider answers passed through
findings.where: src/backend/src/routes/tts.js, services/ai/AIProviderService.js and providers, routes/aiAssistant.js, routes/ai.js
findings.evidence: Code read and test against a local stand-in: (1) no outside call had a time limit, so a provider that hangs holds the request open until the host kills it; (2) the speech route passed the provider's own status to the browser, and the screens treat any 401 as "your session ended", so a wrong provider key signed the user out; (3) the AI routes returned the provider's error text to the caller; (4) the first characters of the speech key were written to the log and returned by a test route; (5) the AI client library retried on its own, with no bound set by us.
findings.expected: Every outside call has a time limit, a bounded number of tries, a breaker, and a plain answer of our own on failure.
findings.actual: None of these.
findings.impact: A slow provider ties up the server; a provider fault signs users out; provider messages and part of a key leak.
findings.correction: One guard for every outside call (lib/outbound.js): time limit, at most five tries and only where the caller marks the call as safe to repeat, a breaker per service, and counters for the integration report. A provider failure is answered 502, 503 or 504 with a sentence written here. The key is no longer logged or returned. The library's own retries are turned off.
findings.requiredTests: Hang, error, wrong key, repeated failure and recovery, each against a stand-in.

findings.cause: The invoice step runs after the dispatch commits and its failure was caught and dropped.
findings.statusNote: On the QA database the list also shows 51 seeded demo orders that the seed never billed. How many live orders are in this state is NOT VERIFIED (no access); the report will show it once deployed.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "shipping succeeds and billing fails: the gap is said, recorded, reported and closed". qa/sim/ui-integration.cjs: "part of a step failed" (3 checks).
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs with billing made to fail for one order: the dispatch answered 200 with no invoice and no word about it. The failure went to the server console only. Nothing listed orders that had shipped and were never billed.
findings.expected: The truck leaving is not undone by a billing fault, but the gap is said, recorded and listed until it is closed.
findings.actual: Silent.
findings.impact: Material leaves and is never billed, and nobody knows.
findings.correction: The dispatch answer carries a warning in words; the shipment screen shows it; an audit entry INVOICE_NOT_RAISED and a structured log line are written; the integration report lists every order shipped but not invoiced, newest first, with the count under "Needs action".
findings.requiredTests: Forced billing failure: stock and order move, warning shown, listed, then closed by raising the invoice.

findings.verification: qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "a revoked key, a suspended partner and a wrong secret all stop at once and say the same little", "staff and partner credentials do not work on each other's API".
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: Code read and test: the token route answered differently for an unknown key, a revoked key and a wrong secret, so a caller could learn which key ids exist and their state; the secret was compared only after the key was found, so timing differed too. A token stayed valid until it expired after its key was revoked. The accepted signing algorithm was not pinned.
findings.expected: One answer for every failed sign-in; a revoked key stops at once.
findings.actual: Three answers; up to an hour of use after revocation.
findings.impact: Key enumeration; a leaked key cannot be cut off promptly.
findings.correction: The secret is always checked, against a dummy hash when the key is unknown, and every failure gets the same answer. Each call checks that the key behind the token is still active (401 KEY_REVOKED). The algorithm is fixed to HS256.
findings.requiredTests: Unknown, revoked, expired and wrong-secret sign-ins are indistinguishable; a revoked key's token is refused on the next call.

findings.workflow: Where events may be sent and how they are signed
findings.statusNote: The public-address rule is on only when NODE_ENV is production, so the local stand-in can be used in tests. The rule itself is unit tested with production set.
findings.verification: test/webhookRules.test.js (6 tests). qa/sim/phase4-integration.mjs: "a webhook address must be one this server may call", "a partner address that redirects is not followed", "a forged, altered or old event fails the signature check a receiver would make".
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.category: Security: request forgery from the server; replay
findings.evidence: Code read: a partner could register any address, including one inside the host's network; redirects were followed; the signature covered the body only, so a captured event could be sent again later and still verify.
findings.expected: Events go to public https addresses only, redirects are not followed, and a signature is tied to its time.
findings.actual: None of the three.
findings.impact: A partner key could be used to make the server call internal addresses; a receiver could not tell a replay.
findings.correction: In production an address must be https and public, checked when registered and again when sent (the name is resolved); a redirect is a failed delivery; a second header X-SteelWise-Signature-Timestamp signs the time with the body. The older header is still sent, unchanged, for receivers already using it.
findings.requiredTests: Private and redirecting addresses refused; forged, altered and old events fail verification.

findings.workflow: What a screen does when the server is slow, silent or gone
findings.statusNote: The late-answer guard and the re-read after a lost answer were added to the shipping screens, which the test drives. Other list screens share the time limit, the messages and the request keys through the API client; their own late-answer handling was not audited one by one.
findings.verification: qa/sim/ui-integration.cjs: 33 checks, 0 failed (7 fail with the four changed files reverted).
findings.phase: Phase 4: API contracts, external integrations, event reliability, error recovery and cross-module communication
findings.evidence: qa/sim/ui-integration.cjs on the code before: 7 of 33 checks fail. A request had no time limit and waited for ever; a lost connection showed nothing or the words "Network Error"; an answer for an old search arriving late replaced the list for the current one; after a step whose answer was lost, the screen kept showing the old state; dispatch, delivery and work order completion are sent with PUT and carried no request key.
findings.expected: A time limit, a sentence that says what happened and what to check, the newest filter wins, and the screen re-reads the record after a lost answer.
findings.actual: As above.
findings.impact: People wait on a dead request, repeat a step that was saved, or act on a stale list.
findings.correction: A 60-second limit on every request; a plain sentence for "no answer" and "took too long" that tells the user it may have been saved; list loads are numbered so a late answer is dropped; after a lost answer the shipment screen reads the shipment again; PUT steps that must not run twice carry a request key.
findings.requiredTests: The ten cases of Phase 4 section 7 in a browser.

findings.category: Contract: limit ignored; reply larger than needed
findings.evidence: Phase 3 measured 244 KB for 50 orders. The routes ignored ?limit and ?offset, always returned their fixed maximum, and gave no total, so a screen could not page (E-021, B-012, G-014).
findings.expected: A caller can ask for a page and learn how many there are, without the body changing shape for existing screens.
findings.actual: Fixed maximum, no total.

findings.correction: The bare-array body is kept. limit and offset are honoured up to the route maximum; X-Total-Count, X-Limit and X-Offset carry the window. GET /api/orders?view=summary returns the header, the customer and a line count instead of every line. A call with no parameters answers exactly as before.

findings.where: src/backend/src/lib/outbound.js (breaker and counters), middleware rate limits, partner rate limit
findings.evidence: Code read: the breaker for outside services, its counters on the integration report, and the staff and partner request limits all live in the memory of one server instance. On a host that runs several instances each keeps its own.
findings.expected: A limit that holds across instances, or a stated bound.

findings.verification: qa/sim/phase5-sales.mjs: "a request for quote keeps grade, size, tolerances, certificates and processing", "request to quote to order: every requirement, the branch, the tax and the links arrive", "a quote line can change a requirement", "a quoted order is reserved, shipped and invoiced with the quote's tax"; src/backend/test/lineSpecs.test.js (5 tests); qa/sim/ui-phase5.cjs: the request and quote screens show the requirements and "subtotal + tax = total". On the code before, the same scenarios fail on every requirement and on tax.
findings.phase: Phase 5: customer lifecycle, sales operations, CRM, quoting, order intake, POS, ecommerce and customer portal
findings.category: Lost customer requirements; wrong tax and branch
findings.evidence: Probe on the QA database, before: a request line kept only a description, quantity and unit, so grade, size, tolerances, certificates and processing typed at the request were nowhere on the quote or the order. A quote saved no tax; the order made from it was untaxed unless someone edited it. The order was filed under the branch of the person who pressed accept, not the branch that owned the request.
findings.expected: What the customer asked for is typed once and reaches the quote, the order and the shop floor; a quote shows tax by rule 27 and the order carries it; the order belongs to the request's branch.
findings.actual: Requirements, tax and branch were dropped at each step.
findings.impact: Wrong material or missing certificates shipped; untaxed orders; orders filed and reported under the wrong branch.
findings.correction: Request lines keep the requirements (validated, stored in their existing JSON column). Quote and order lines get them in their own columns, the quote line may change any of them, the order line keeps the grade record. A quote is taxed by rule 27 at the request's branch and keeps tax and total; acceptance carries them and files the order under the request's branch. No schema change.
findings.requiredTests: Requirements, tax, branch and links checked on the saved rows from request to order and invoice; a bad requirement refused with the field named.

findings.evidence: Schema and code read, and qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs "the Steel Outlet remnant list is separate from stock": the outlet's Remnant table has no link to a stock item, its "reserve" is a flag, and reserving or selling one moves no stock balance. Remnants made by a work order or entered against a parent are stock items and are fully traced; the outlet list is a different list of the same kind of material.
findings.expected: One stock list (owner decision 1): an outlet remnant is a stock item, and selling it takes it off the books.
findings.actual: A separate list.
findings.impact: A remnant can be sold at the outlet and still be on the books, or the reverse. Includes J-012 (the counter remnant quick-add).
findings.correction: Make the outlet list a view of stock items that are remnants (parent item set, or flagged), keep its pricing fields beside the item, and make reserve and sale use the stock reservation and counter-sale rules. The outlet price of a remnant needs the owner's rule first (S-009: the 15% and 25% discounts fixed in code).
findings.requiredTests: A remnant sold at the outlet leaves the books once and returns on a void.

findings.statusNote: Owner's decision 9, 2026-11-15: (1) Cost: actual cost per item, taken from the purchase order line at receipt; pieces cut from an item carry its cost per pound; a job costs the material its work orders used plus the time on its steps at a rate the owner enters per kind of work center; no overhead; no rate is invented. (2) A coil work order can be raised for a job, and the job shows material used, made, scrap and yield. (3) Sending a job for rework adds a rework step that is started and clocked like any step. (4) Every job passes inspection before packing unless its routing is marked "no inspection". (5) A certification is required where the kind of work center is marked; one operator on two steps at once only where marked; clocks running longer than 12 hours are listed for the supervisor. (6) Each kind of work center can carry its own inspection checklist, entered by the owner; the standard list is used until then. Owner decision 9 (2026-11-15): actual cost per item. A receipt against a purchase order line now records the item's cost per stocked unit from the line's price (per hundredweight, pound or ton for stock kept in pounds; each for stock kept in pieces). Pieces cut by a work order and pieces received from a parent carry the parent's cost. A price that cannot be turned into a unit cost (for example per foot for stock kept in pounds) leaves the cost empty. Still open: stock already on hand has no cost unless typed; landed cost (freight, duty) is not worked out; stock movements carry no value, so scrap, shortage and count variance have no amount; Inventory.avgCost is still never written; there is no valuation report. These belong to Phase 8 (accounting). Phase 8: shipment movements now carry the item's unit cost (N-017). A valuation report and a ledger are not built (N-025).
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "an item's cost is taken from its purchase order line when it is received, and the pieces cut from it carry the same cost per pound"; qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs "receiving records the cost from the purchase order line". Mutation: 2 rules removed in turn, group 6 fails each time.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.where: Inventory.unitCost, landedCost, avgCost; Coil.unitCost, landedCost; lib/receiving.js
findings.evidence: Schema and code read, and qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs "receiving does not create a cost": a receipt records no cost, even against a purchase order line that has a price. Cost is typed on the item by a manager afterwards. Inventory.avgCost is never written. No movement carries a value, so scrap, shortage, count variance and cost of goods sold have no amount.
findings.expected: A costing method chosen by the owner (actual cost per item, average, or standard), applied at receipt and carried by every movement.
findings.actual: No cost unless typed by hand.
findings.impact: Inventory value, margin and the cost of scrap and shortages cannot be reported from the records.
findings.correction: Not made: the instruction forbids changing costing rules without authorisation. Recommended: actual cost per item from the purchase order line at receipt (steel is bought and traced by the item), landed cost added when freight is known, pieces inherit cost by weight.
findings.requiredTests: Per the decision: receipt, cut, scrap, transfer and shipment each carry the value; the sum of item values equals the ledger.

findings.statusNote: Question for the owner: how often is each class of stock counted, and what size of variance needs a manager's approval?
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.evidence: Code read: a manager or the inventory manager can correct one item to a counted quantity with a note, and the count is recorded. There is no count sheet, no schedule, no blind count, no recount and no threshold above which a variance needs a second person.
findings.expected: A count program whose frequency, tolerance and approval the owner sets.
findings.actual: Single-item correction only.
findings.impact: Counts are done item by item with no record of what was due or missed.
findings.correction: Not built: the frequency, the variance that needs approval and who approves are the owner's. The single-item count, its refusals and its record are verified.
findings.requiredTests: Per the decision.

findings.statusNote: Question for the owner: do the branches want bins on file (each branch supplies its list), or is a typed bin enough?
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.where: Location table (85 rows, all branches); Coil.binLocation (free text)
findings.evidence: Database read: every Location row is a branch. A bin is free text on the item, so two spellings of one bin are two bins, a bin that does not exist is accepted, and nothing lists what is in a bin except a text search.
findings.expected: Bins on file per branch, chosen from a list.
findings.actual: Free text.
findings.impact: Slower picking and mis-typed bins; no capacity or zone rules possible.
findings.correction: Not built in this phase: a bin master needs each branch's real layout, which is not on file. Putaway to a typed bin is verified.

findings.statusNote: The supply position is VERIFIED. Question for the owner: is a reorder point wanted per grade and branch, and who sets it?
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs: "the supply position shows what is on order and moves it to on hand when it arrives", "the supply position keeps to the branch the person works at, and suggests nothing"; qa/sim/ui-phase6.cjs: "supply position: rows for my branch only".
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.where: new GET /api/purchase-orders/supply-position; Purchase orders screen, Supply position tab
findings.evidence: Schema and code read: only spare parts have a reorder point. For material there was nothing: no minimum, no maximum, no view of what is on order or coming by transfer against open sales.
findings.expected: The buyer sees the position per branch and grade, and reorder levels the owner sets raise suggestions.
findings.actual: Nothing.

findings.correction: Built: the supply position (on hand, free, reserved, on hold, sent in transit, on order, coming by transfer, open sales not reserved, projected free), kept to the person's branches. Not built: minimums, maximums and suggested orders, which are the owner's numbers. No purchase order is created by the system.

findings.workflow: Receiving against a purchase order line
findings.statusNote: Questions for the owner: what over-receipt is accepted without a hold (for example 5% or 10%), and does a purchase order above some value need approval before it is placed?
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.evidence: Built in this phase with the narrowest rule that invents nothing: a receipt is compared with the line as written. Size is held to the tolerance on the line and is exact when the line gives none; any quantity over the line is an over-receipt; a mismatch is received on hold, never refused.
findings.expected: The owner's receiving tolerances: how much over or under a line is acceptable, and whether a mismatch is held or refused.
findings.actual: Exact, held.
findings.impact: More holds than the business may want (a mill shipping 2% over is normal), until a tolerance is set.
findings.correction: A percentage over-receipt tolerance and a default size tolerance, once the owner gives them. No approval step for purchase orders was invented either.
findings.requiredTests: Per the decision.

findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer

findings.expected: A supplier invoice is checked against the order and the receipts before it is paid.
findings.actual: Not recorded.
findings.impact: Payables are checked outside the system.

deferral.targetPhase: The phase the owner issues for finance, costing and supplier invoices
deferral.correction: A supplier invoice record matched to purchase order lines and receipts, with the costing decision K-007.

deferral.verification: A scenario that receives short and invoices in full.

findings.workflow: Finding an item by scanning its tag
findings.statusNote: HARDWARE NOT VERIFIED: blocked on access to the scanners, printers and readers the branches use. No claim of compatibility with any scanner, printer or reader is made.
