findings.workflow: How an item in transit is shown in lists
findings.statusNote: Phase 9: a stock item on its way to another branch says "In Transit" on its row in the stock list. The list answer now carries the stock record's state.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase9-ui.cjs: "an item on its way to another branch says In Transit on its row in the stock list (K-014)"; qa/tools/phase9-mutations.cjs 25.
findings.phase: Phase 9: user interface, user experience, design system, role workspaces, navigation, responsive design, accessibility and interaction verification
findings.evidence: An item in transit keeps its item status (for example AVAILABLE) and its balance carries the in-transit state. The item's own page says it is in transit and switches Move off; the stock list shows the item status and a free quantity of 0.
findings.expected: The list says "in transit" on the row.
findings.actual: Shown on the item page and the Transfers screen only.
findings.impact: A person reading only the list sees an available item with nothing free.

findings.workflow: A hold or release at the same moment as another change to the same item
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase6-inventory.mjs: "a hold queues behind a stock change in progress on the same item instead of deadlocking" (with the lock removed the hold answers 500; with it, 201), "a hold racing counts and cuts on the same item never ends in a server error" (144 requests on 12 items) and "forty stock changes at once leave every balance in step".
findings.phase: Phase 6: inventory, purchasing, receiving, reservations, replenishment, material traceability, remnants, scrap and interbranch transfer
findings.evidence: Second full gate run of Phase 6, scenario "forty stock changes at once": one hold answered 500. The server log shows PostgreSQL error 40P01, deadlock detected: the hold had updated the item and was waiting for its balance while a count correction held the balance and was waiting for the item.
findings.expected: Every stock change takes the balance row first and the item second, so two changes queue.
findings.actual: A hold and a release took the item first. The database ended one of the two transactions; nothing was saved wrongly, and the person saw "Could not place the hold".
findings.impact: Rare: needs two people changing one item in the same instant. No balance was wrong. The person had to try again with no explanation.
findings.correction: placeHold and releaseHold lock the balance row first, like lib/stockChanges.js and lib/transfers.js.
findings.requiredTests: Holds and releases raced against counts and cuts on the same items, many at once: no server error, books in balance.

findings.cause: Job status and inspection result were two unconnected records; five routes each changed the status in their own way.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a job waiting for inspection cannot be released by hand", "a job that failed inspection cannot be packed, shipped or completed by any route until a new inspection passes", "sent for rework, a job goes back to the floor with the instructions and must pass a new inspection"; src/backend/test/phase7Rules.test.js; with the gate removed two quality scenarios fail (mutation run); qa/tools/db-facts.mjs "jobs past inspection whose latest decided inspection failed" at 0.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.where: src/backend/src/routes/jobs.js (every status address); new src/backend/src/lib/jobGates.js and lib/productionRules.js
findings.evidence: Probe on the QA database, before: a sales login moved a job from waiting for inspection to ready to ship with no inspection on file (200). After an inspection failed, the same login moved the job from on hold to ready to ship (200). A job sent back for rework was started and completed straight to ready to ship with no second inspection (200).
findings.expected: Only a passed inspection moves a job on from inspection, and a job whose last inspection failed cannot be packed, shipped or completed until a new inspection passes.
findings.actual: The job move table allowed the moves and nothing looked at the inspections.
findings.impact: Material that was never inspected, or that failed inspection, could be shipped to a customer.
findings.correction: Every job status change now goes through one function (changeJobStatusTx) that locks the job and applies the quality gate: no release with an inspection open, none after a failed inspection, none from the inspection queue without a pass recorded since the job arrived there. "Complete" on a reworked job sends it to inspection.
findings.requiredTests: Each bypass refused at every address and for every role; the legitimate path still works.

findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "an inspection cannot be passed with a required check unanswered or failed, or a measurement out of tolerance", "a conditional pass must state its conditions, keeps the inspector's earlier notes, and cannot carry a disposition that says the material is not going on"; qa/sim/ui-phase7.cjs: the screen refuses a conditional pass with no conditions; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: an inspection with a required check marked FAIL was passed (200). A conditional pass was accepted with no conditions and replaced the inspector's notes. Found while writing the scenarios: a conditional pass could carry the disposition SCRAP or REWORK and still send the job to packaging.
findings.expected: A pass needs every required check answered as passed and no measurement out of tolerance; a conditional pass states its conditions and keeps what the inspector wrote.
findings.actual: The pass address saved whatever it was sent.
findings.impact: A recorded failure could be signed off as a pass; the reason for a concession was lost.
findings.correction: Pass is refused with 409 naming the failed or unanswered check or the measurement out of tolerance. Conditional pass requires conditions, keeps earlier notes beneath them, and accepts only USE_AS_IS or SELL_SECONDARY. Dispositions are validated.
findings.requiredTests: Each refusal leaves the inspection open and the job waiting; the valid cases are saved as entered.

findings.workflow: Opening and deciding inspections at the same moment
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a job has one open inspection at a time, even when two inspectors open one at the same moment", "an inspection passed and failed at the same moment has one result" (6 rounds), "passing an inspection moves the job to packaging in the same step, and records who decided", "an open inspection can be filled in as the inspector goes"; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: two inspections could be opened for one job (201, 201). The decision and the job move were separate writes. The audit log did not say which signed-in person decided. An inspection could name an inspector who is not on file, at creation and (found this phase) by editing.
findings.expected: One open inspection per job; a decision and the job's move are one step; who decided is on record.
findings.actual: No lock and no check.
findings.impact: Two inspectors could reach different results on one job; the job could be left in a state that matched neither.
findings.correction: Opening and deciding lock the job. One open inspection per job. The decision, the job move and an audit row INSPECTION_DECIDED (with the signed-in user, result, disposition and where the job went) are one transaction. The inspector is validated on create and edit; checklist and measurements must be lists.
findings.requiredTests: Pass and fail sent together: one wins and inspection, job, history and audit agree.

findings.workflow: Starting, pausing and finishing a step
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "steps run in their planned order", "the planned-order rule is one setting", "a step that was never started cannot be finished", "finishing the last step sends the job to inspection once; finishing it again changes nothing", "pausing closes the clock with the reason given", "two operators starting the same step at the same moment leave one clock running"; qa/sim/phase2-integrity.mjs (two new checks); mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: step 2 started before step 1 (200); a step that was never started was completed (200); a completed step was started again and went back to in process (200); a step with nothing running was "paused" (200). This is finding B-011 confirmed by running it.
findings.expected: A step is started, then paused or finished; a finished step stays finished; steps follow the planned order if the owner says so.
findings.actual: No check of the step's present state.
findings.impact: Start and end times and labor time could be overwritten or invented; a job could reach inspection with work recorded out of order.
findings.correction: State rules decided on the locked plan: complete requires started, pause requires a running clock, a finished step cannot be restarted, nothing starts on a job that is closed, on hold or past production. Planned order is the owner's decision of 2026-11-15 (decision 8): a step cannot start until the steps before it are finished. The rule is one setting (production.rules.stepsInOrder), on by default.
findings.requiredTests: Each refusal with no clock started; the order rule on, off and by default; two starts at once leave one clock.

findings.workflow: Who and where a step is run
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a step is run only on a work center of its own kind, at the job's branch, that is switched on", "an operator whose certification has lapsed, who is inactive, or who works at another branch cannot start a step", "a step is moved to another work center or operator only where it can be run"; qa/tools/db-facts.mjs "steps running on a work center of another kind, or at another branch"; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: a step of a QA-L01 job was started at a QA-L02 work center by a QA-L02 operator (200). A step could be started on a work center of another kind or one switched off, by an operator whose certification had expired or who was inactive.
findings.expected: A step runs on a work center of its own kind at the job's branch, by an active operator of that branch whose certification for that kind, if on file, has not expired.
findings.actual: Only that the operator and work center existed.
findings.impact: Work recorded at the wrong branch; time booked against a machine that cannot do the step; lapsed certifications ignored.
findings.correction: checkWho() refuses with 409 and a sentence naming the work center, branch, operator or the certification and its expiry date. The same check applies to reassigning a step.
findings.requiredTests: Each refusal; a valid start; a reassign.

findings.workflow: Moving a job out of production
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a job cannot leave production while a planned step is unfinished", "a job put on hold while its last step is running stays on hold when the step is finished"; qa/tools/db-facts.mjs "jobs past production with a planned step unfinished" at 0; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: a job with two planned steps, neither finished, was completed by hand to ready to ship (200).
findings.expected: A job with planned steps leaves production when its steps are finished.
findings.actual: The steps were not consulted.
findings.impact: A job could be shipped with planned work not done and no time recorded.
findings.correction: A move to inspection, packaging, ready to ship, shipped or completed is refused with 409 naming the first open step. Cancelling and holding are still allowed.
findings.requiredTests: Refused at every address; cancel and hold accepted.

findings.workflow: Running the scheduling engine for a branch
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: the first 12 "Capacity planning and scheduling" scenarios; qa/sim/ui-phase7.cjs: the shop-floor screen reports what was placed and what was not, with the reason; src/backend/test/phase7Rules.test.js; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: the run scheduled steps of a cancelled job; it chose an operator whose certification had expired; it considered operators of other branches; it wrote a start time for every step though no duration is on file; it gave no reason for steps it left unplaced. Two runs at once could both place a step. Found while writing the scenarios: a production manager of one branch could run the engine for another branch (200).
findings.expected: Open jobs only, this branch's qualified people and machines, no invented times, a reason for anything unplaced, one run at a time, own branch only.
findings.actual: As described.
findings.impact: Work queued for cancelled jobs; unqualified assignments; start times nobody had grounds for.
findings.correction: The decision is a pure function (planAssignments). The run takes a per-branch lock, places steps of open jobs only, uses this branch's operators with a current certification, skips machines that are off or locked out, writes a start time only for the step at the front of a queue, and returns what it could not place and what it did not check (for example thickness, where a work center has no limit on file). A branch planner gets 403 for another branch. The writes are grouped (one statement per work center, operator and queue position), which took a run at a branch with 7,090 waiting jobs from 45 seconds to under 2. Another branch's run is refused with 403.
findings.requiredTests: Each case; three runs at once place each step once.

findings.workflow: The job planner: preview, apply, what-if
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "the planner takes a job's time from its routing", "a work center with no working hours on file has no utilisation figure", "an overloaded work center is reported as a bottleneck from the figures on file", "applying a schedule saves the work center and times, and counts only what it saved", "a schedule line is refused when the work center is at another branch, the wrong kind, switched off, or the times run backwards", "the planner places a job only at its own branch", "a preview and a what-if save nothing"; qa/sim/ui-phase7.cjs; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Code read and probe, before: every job with no estimate was given 60 minutes and every work center 480 minutes a day, and utilisation was reported from those. Apply wrote whatever the browser sent: a work center at another branch, an end before the start, a job already finished; it answered "applied 2" having checked nothing.
findings.expected: Figures come from the records or are reported as not known; a schedule line is checked on the server before it is saved.
findings.actual: Assumed figures presented as real; an unchecked write.
findings.impact: A capacity picture nobody had entered; jobs moved to machines that could not run them.
findings.correction: A job takes its time from its routing (set-up plus machine minutes) or from its own dates; otherwise it is queued with no start or end. A work center with no hours on file has no utilisation figure. The plan carries notes saying what is not counted. Apply checks each line against the job and work center as they are now, saves only jobs still waiting to start, and reports the true count with a reason for each line skipped.
findings.requiredTests: Routing time, no time, no hours, overload, apply refusals, branch.

findings.workflow: Counts and lists shown to planners and inspectors
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "the late-jobs list puts overdue first, includes jobs waiting for inspection, and refuses a nonsense time window", "the quality figures are counted from the records", "the shop-floor figures count work still to do on open jobs only, and agree with the queue", "leadership sees production at every branch" (branch counts equal the records); qa/sim/ui-phase7.cjs; mutation run.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: job counts for a named branch answered 500. The late-jobs list left out jobs waiting for inspection, in packaging or on hold, and its sort compared missing values. The quality pass rate read 100% on a day with no decisions. Found this phase: the shop-floor figures counted waiting steps of cancelled and held jobs as work to do, so they disagreed with the queue beside them.
findings.expected: Each figure equals a count of the records, and "not known" is shown as such.
findings.actual: As described.
findings.impact: Planners and managers reading wrong numbers.
findings.correction: The inspection queue lists the most urgent first (it listed the least urgent first), and the inspection queue, the steps list and the late list are capped with the total stated, so a large branch gets a short answer. The branch filter is fixed; the late list covers every unfinished status, overdue first, and refuses a nonsense window; the pass rate is null (shown as a dash) when nothing was decided; the shop-floor figures count work to do on open jobs only.
findings.requiredTests: Each figure compared with a direct count.

findings.workflow: Values filled in when none was entered
findings.statusNote: The plan's thickness column does not accept "empty", so "not stated" is saved as 0 (L-029).
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a plan takes the grade and thickness from the order line and assumes neither", "a suggested routing names steps only: no times or tolerances are made up", "a work center's recorded thickness limit is respected, and where none is recorded the answer says thickness was not checked"; qa/sim/ui-phase7.cjs: a new work center starts with no thickness limit.
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Probe, before: a plan for a job with no grade or thickness was saved as grade A36, thickness 0.5 in. A work center with no type was reported as a saw, with a division and a 12 in thickness limit; the new work center window started at 12 in. The routing suggestion returned minutes and tolerances that came from nowhere.
findings.expected: What is not known is saved and shown as not known.
findings.actual: Defaults that read as facts.
findings.impact: Steps matched to machines on a made-up thickness; routings carrying made-up times.
findings.correction: A plan takes grade and thickness from the job or its order line, else no grade and thickness 0 (not stated). A work center reports only what is on its record. The suggestion names steps only, with times 0 and tolerances empty, and says so. The window starts with no limit.
findings.requiredTests: Each case reads back as entered or as not stated.

findings.verification: qa/sim/phase7-manufacturing.mjs: "a routing goes draft, review, in use; only a routing in use can be put on a job", "a routing step must have a name, a kind of work center on file, its own place in the order and times that are not negative", "a routing with no steps cannot go into use", "the routing offered for a material is one that is in use", "sales staff can read routings but cannot create, change or put one into use".
findings.phase: Phase 7: manufacturing execution, work orders, routing, capacity planning, scheduling, shop-floor operations, quality control, material consumption, remnants, rework and operational intelligence
findings.evidence: Code read and probe: a routing with no steps could be made active; a step could name a kind of work center that is not on file, share a sequence number with another, or carry negative minutes; a status change was read-then-write.
findings.expected: An active routing has at least one valid step; status moves draft, review, active, retired, one at a time.
findings.actual: No validation.
findings.impact: A job could be given a routing that cannot be run.

findings.cause: A deadlock met by one of the database client's own statements is reported with no error code, only the database's words, so the retry did not recognise it; and the order save had no retry.
findings.verification: qa/sim/phase8-fulfillment.mjs: "an order cancelled at the very moment its shipment is dispatched ends one way or the other, never half of each" now also checks that no request is answered with a server error; src/backend/test/phase8Rules.test.js (overlap forms). With the recognition removed the scenario fails. The order-save retry was run 36 rounds with no error; without it one round in about twelve failed, so its removal is not a reliable mutation and is not counted.
findings.phase: Phase 8: shipping, packaging, dispatch, logistics, delivery, invoicing, financial reconciliation, order costing and customer order closeout
findings.evidence: Found by reading the server log of the first full Phase 8 regression run: six dispatch requests answered 500 in the scenario that cancels an order while its shipment is dispatched. The database had stopped one of the two saves as a deadlock (the cancel releases the reserved stock while the dispatch takes it). The scenario itself had passed, because the records were right in every round: the save that lost was rolled back whole. A later run showed the cancel side answering 500 the same way.
findings.expected: The save that loses is run again and its user is told plainly what happened (409).
findings.actual: A 500 with "Failed to dispatch" or "Failed to update order". Nothing was half-saved.
findings.impact: Rare: needs a cancel and a dispatch of the same order within the same fraction of a second. The user saw an error and had to look again. No record was wrong.
findings.correction: The retry recognises this third form of the same event, and the order save uses the retry. The loser now answers 409.
findings.requiredTests: Cancel and dispatch together, many rounds: every answer is 200 or 409.
